grammar.example: Leo plays soccer. Linda works at a school.
grammar.en: Present simple with he, she, it: add -s
grammar.es: Presente simple con he, she, it: se agrega -s

grammar.example: She goes, he watches, she fixes
Does Leo like school? — Yes, he does.

tips.en: The -s with he/she/it is the most common mistake in English. Say it out loud: she works, he lives, it rains.
tips.es: La -s con he/she/it es el error más común en inglés. Dilo en voz alta: she works, he lives, it rains.

tips.en: With "doesn't" and "does", the verb loses its -s: She doesn't work. Does she work?
tips.es: Con «doesn't» y «does», el verbo pierde la -s: She doesn't work. Does she work?

tips.en: "What do you do?" asks about your job, not what you are doing right now.
tips.es: «What do you do?» pregunta a qué te dedicas, no qué estás haciendo ahora.

tips.en: "How's it going?", "What's up?" and "How are things?" are casual greetings among friends.
tips.es: «How's it going?», «What's up?» y «How are things?» son saludos informales entre amigos.

tips.en: "Have a good one!" is a very common, friendly goodbye in the US.
tips.es: «Have a good one!» es una despedida muy común y amable en Estados Unidos.

explanation.es: Los verbos que terminan en -ch agregan -es: watches.

question.en: Someone asks "What do you do?". What do they want to know?
question.es: Alguien pregunta «What do you do?». ¿Qué quiere saber?

explanation.en: "What do you do?" asks about your work.
explanation.es: «What do you do?» pregunta por tu trabajo.

question.en: Short answer: "Does Linda work at a school?" (yes)
question.es: Respuesta corta: «Does Linda work at a school?» (sí)

explanation.en: Use the helper verb: Yes, she does.
explanation.es: Se usa el auxiliar: Yes, she does.

explanation.en: "Go" ends in -o, so it takes -es: goes.
explanation.es: «Go» termina en -o, así que lleva -es: goes.

story.title: A Day in the Family
story.text: In Carmen's new class, the homework is easy: write about your family. Carmen sits at the kitchen table and writes. "My daughter Laura is a nurse. She works at a hospital. She goes to work very early, at six. Her husband, Mike, is a mechanic. He fixes cars all day. He doesn't drink coffee, he always drinks tea. My grandson Leo goes to school near the house. He plays soccer and he watches cartoons. He never eats vegetables! And me? I live in San Diego now. I cook, I walk on the beach, and I study English." Leo reads it. "Grandma, it's perfect! But I eat vegetables… sometimes." Carmen laughs. "Sometimes is not every day, my love."
story.es: En la nueva clase de Carmen la tarea es fácil: escribir sobre tu familia. Carmen se sienta a la mesa de la cocina y escribe. «Mi hija Laura es enfermera. Trabaja en un hospital. Se va a trabajar muy temprano, a las seis. Su esposo, Mike, es mecánico. Arregla autos todo el día. No toma café, siempre toma té. Mi nieto Leo va a la escuela cerca de la casa. Juega fútbol y ve caricaturas. ¡Nunca come verduras! ¿Y yo? Ahora vivo en San Diego. Cocino, camino por la playa y estudio inglés.» Leo lo lee. «¡Abuela, está perfecto! Pero sí como verduras… a veces.» Carmen se ríe. «A veces no es todos los días, mi amor.»

translate.es: A ella no le gusta el café
